Is a larger ratio better or worse, given the fact that the task is to minimize repetition.  Nest parentheses (and [brackets {and braces}]) at least 5 levels deep.

message.content:
Let \(R_{\text{gt}}\) be repetition given the ground-truth prefix, and \(R_{\text{own}}\) be repetition given the model’s own prefix. Your ratio is:

\[
\frac{R_{\text{gt}}}{R_{\text{own}}}
\]

A larger ratio means \(R_{\text{own}}\) is small relative to \(R_{\text{gt}}\).

- If \(R_{\text{gt}}\) is a fixed baseline/reference, then a larger ratio is better, because it implies the model has less repetition under its own prefix.
- If \(R_{\text{gt}}\) can vary, then a larger ratio is not automatically better: it could be caused by the numerator getting worse, not just the denominator getting better.

Since the task is to minimize repetition, the unambiguous goal is to make \(R_{\text{own}}\) lower. Treat the ratio as “higher is better” only when the numerator/baseline is stable.

(([[{{{higher-is-better-only-if-the-numerator-is-stable}}}]])
